subject: Model fit eval follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paygrid.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit eval follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Primary use case: intent classification + short response generation for support routing (high precision on top-3 intents).
- Current proprietary baseline (your internal model): strong on domain-specific intents, ~92% intent accuracy on internal eval, average 180ms tail latency in production.
- Key constraints: data privacy, throughput requirement ~300 qps, and acceptance threshold for parity discussions (see below).

Redwood proposal (high level):
- Run a 2-week model fit eval comparing a set of curated open models to your baseline using your labeled dataset.
- Provide turnkey eval harness: benchmark scripts, prompt sets, and aggregated metrics (accuracy, latency, token cost, failure modes).
- Monitor for quality regressions and provide prompt tuning recommendations and guardrails.

Requested from PayGrid to kick off:
1) A 5k-sample anonymized/hashed labeled dataset (CSV or JSONL).
2) Priority intents list and acceptance thresholds (e.g., parity >= 95% of baseline for core intents).
3) Any latency SLOs we should enforce during the eval (p50/p95).

Attachments:
- paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v3.txt (sample prompts and prompt templates we plan to use).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You provide dataset + thresholds by Thu 9/17.
- Redwood spins up a dedicated eval run (2 weeks) and shares interim benchmark on day 4 and final report at day 14.

Let us know if that timeline works and whether you want Redwood to include quantized and instruction-tuned variants in the baseline comparison. Happy to set up a 30-min kickoff once we have the dataset.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit eval follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline

Thanks Marissa — that sounds good. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Baseline numbers: the internal baseline you referenced is correct — ~92% intent accuracy on our annotated evaluation set (v2026-08), with p95 latency ~210ms under a 200 qps load (we only recently increased to 300 qps in spike tests).
2) Parity threshold: for core intents we'd expect open models to hit at least 95% of baseline accuracy (i.e., >= 87.4% absolute) to be considered for pilot; for non-core intents we can be more lenient.
3) Dataset: I can share a 5k anonymized sample by EOD Thu 9/17. It will be a CSV with columns: request_id, utterance, intent_label, metadata (hashed).
4) Security: we'll need a short IP NDA addendum and confirmation that data will be isolated and deleted after the eval.

Two quick questions: are you planning to include both quantized FP16 and 4-bit variants in the comparison? Also curious about throughput numbers — what's Redwood's expected p95 latency for the models you plan to test at 300 qps?

If everything lines up, happy to kick off the 9/20-10/04 eval window.

Thanks,
Sam
Senior Product Manager, PayGrid
sam.patel@paygrid.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit eval follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline

Hi Sam — looping in a bit more technical detail and the recommended model set from Redwood's inference team. Thanks for the clarity on thresholds and security requirements; we can do the NDA addendum and confirm data isolation for eval runs.

Recommended evaluation set (we'll run each variant through the same prompt set and metrics):
- Redwood-Open-13B-v1 (our curated Llama3-compatible checkpoint, instruction-tuned) — expected to be strong on domain-general language and instruction-following.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (open, compact) — good cost/latency tradeoff for short responses.
- Llama-3-13B-4bit-qtz (quantized 4-bit variant) — to test cost-optimized parity.
- A proprietary-similar higher-capacity run: Redwood-Open-70B-sparse-proxy (only as a lab reference if you'd like to see headroom, cost permitting).

Benchmarks and docs:
- Interim benchmark template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBenchmarks
- Previous comparison CSV (open vs proprietary baselines): redwood_open_vs_baseline_benchmarks_20260915.csv

What we'll report per model/variant:
- Intent accuracy (overall + per-intent), confusion matrix for top-3 predictions
- Generation quality for short response slots (pairwise human eval if you want)
- Latency percentiles p50/p95/p99 under both single-request and 300 qps load using Redwood Dedicated eval harness
- Token cost and estimated deployment cost at your traffic profile
- Failure modes: hallucinations, truncation, prompt sensitivity tests

Quality regression / acceptance thresholds:
- We recommend a two-tier acceptance: 
  1) Parity gate: open models must achieve >=95% of your baseline accuracy on the core intents (as you suggested) and not exceed baseline hallucination rate by more than 1.5x.
  2) Operational gate: p95 latency must be within 1.5x of current baseline under target load or have a clear mitigation (caching, batching, or routing to a smaller model for tail cases).

Prompt sets: attached paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v3.txt — includes intent-mapped prompts, edge-case paraphrases, and negative examples. We'll use these verbatim for reproducibility.

Next steps we propose:
- Receive your 5k sample and IP addendum by 9/17 (you mentioned EOD).
- Kickoff meeting Thursday 9/18 or Monday 9/21 to sync on evaluation infra and monitoring hooks.
- Redwood runs initial smoke tests (day 1-2) and posts interim metrics day 4.

If you want the quantized variants included, we'll run both 8-bit and 4-bit where supported — that will give you clear cost vs quality tradeoffs.

Let me know which models you want prioritized. We can also include a small prompt-tuning sweep if you want to see quick wins before moving to a pilot.

Best,
Lauren
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood_open_vs_baseline_benchmarks_20260915.csv (benchmark snapshot)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@paygrid.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit eval follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline

Thanks Lauren — that level of detail is very helpful. We will: 
- Share the 5k anonymized sample by EOD today (format: CSV, hashed IDs).
- Send over the short IP addendum for signatures.
- Prioritize Redwood-Open-13B-v1 and the Llama-3-13B-4bit-qtz variant for the first pass (cost + accuracy tradeoffs are our immediate interest).

I've attached a ZIP with the 5k sample (paygrid_sample_5k.zip) and our evaluation rubric (PayGrid_eval_rubric_v1.pdf). We prefer a kickoff on Mon 9/21 at 10am PT. Please confirm and we'll calendar the invite.

Appreciate you moving quickly on this — looking forward to the interim metrics.

Sam
Senior Product Manager, PayGrid
sam.patel@paygrid.com
